post.caption: MoMA showed a sink strainer necklace. Bauhaus weaver Anni Albers made jewelry with her student Alex Reed, inspired by ancient jewels from a tomb in Mexico. She said jewelry usually meant gold and silver, pearls or diamonds, so they shopped at hardware stores and five and dime stores for washers and paper clips. Their best known necklace hangs paper clips from a sink strainer. In 1946, MoMA's Modern Handmade Jewelry show included their pieces. The Albers Foundation in Connecticut keeps the necklace.
